# Relay branding policy

**ADOPTED — Version 1.1. Effective date: 2026-11-19.** The owner explicitly approved this policy and the separate artwork copyright grant. Version 1.0, effective 2026-11-18, is retained in licenses/BRANDING-v1.0.md as the prior policy record.

## Source code, artwork copyright, and product identity

Approved original Relay source and explicitly scoped test data remain MPL-2.0. Modified forks may use, modify, sell and redistribute that code according to its license. The existing thirteen icon files in `licenses/BRANDING_ASSET_MANIFEST.json` remain outside MPL; their copyright permissions are the separate MIT/Expat terms in ARTWORK_LICENSE.md. These copyright rights include making and distributing artwork modifications without separate approval.

The Relay name and official monitor/phone/arrow logo are used as product identifiers. This policy addresses their use as branding and claims about origin or endorsement. It grants only rights actually held by the project; it does not claim ownership of the ordinary word “relay,” registered trademarks, exclusive copyright, worldwide trademark priority, or independently verified third-party clearance.

## Product-identity permissions

- Unmodified, genuine Relay builds may retain the original name and icons. A genuine build is compiled from an identified, unmodified Relay source version; ordinary build configuration, dependency selection and packaging metadata changes are permitted when they do not misrepresent behavior or origin. An independent distributor must identify itself and must not imply official release status, endorsement or support merely from using the branding.
- Source forks may retain original branding assets for completeness, attribution and reproducibility without implying endorsement or official status. Source retention does not itself grant product-identity permission for a distributed modified application.
- Independently distributed modified applications must use a distinguishable product name and icon unless separately authorized to use the official branding. This is a condition of the project's permission to use its product identifiers as marks, to the extent enforceable under applicable trademark law; it is not a copyright condition on exercising rights under MIT, MPL or GPL. Merely adding “Unofficial” does not grant permission to use an otherwise confusing product identity.
- Descriptive derivative names such as **Relay-Python** are permitted for unofficial forks with distinct visual branding and clear identification as independent projects. Such a presentation satisfies the distinguishable-name permission and does not imply endorsement.
- Independently created branding inspired by Relay's general design concepts is permitted when sufficiently distinguishable and not presented as official or endorsed. Copyright-authorized artwork modifications may likewise be made; their use as a product identifier must respect applicable trademark/origin law and these limited branding permissions.
- Technical renditions for authorized branding use, including resizing, rasterization and platform packaging, are permitted. Preserve applicable copyright/license notices. A genuine build using the official branding should preserve this policy as the statement of its branding permission.
- Truthful attribution, discussion, reviews and accurate screenshots/logo reproductions to identify Relay are permitted without implying endorsement. Nothing here overrides fair use, descriptive use or other rights available under applicable law.

Do not misrepresent another product or a modified build as the official Relay application, claim endorsement without agreement, or present a redesigned logo as an official Relay mark. Modified material should be identified reasonably as modified and its origin should not be misrepresented. This is origin protection, not a restriction on changing or redistributing copyright-licensed material.

## Copyright-license priority and limits of enforcement

Nothing in this policy limits rights granted under MIT, MPL or GPL or adds a further copyright restriction to a GPL-covered work. The separate artwork copyright permission is not conditioned on surrendering GPL rights or accepting additional contractual limitations. A lack of trademark permission does not revoke copyright permissions. Where applicable law independently permits a use of a mark, this document does not remove that right. The project does not promise that every desired name/icon distinction can be enforced everywhere in the absence of valid trademark or misrepresentation rights.

## Provenance and limitations

The documented sequence is one owner-provided reference depicting the previous Relay design, a ChatGPT-generated improved logo, an icon-only/background-removal refinement, and Codex SVG conversion/application renditions. There was not a second owner-supplied reference. The extent of protectable authorship and the earlier reference's independent rights have not been conclusively verified. AI generation/vectorization does not establish exclusive ownership or third-party clearance. Any grant is limited to rights the grantor actually holds; applicable third-party rights remain unaffected.

No warranty of title, non-infringement or fitness is offered to the extent applicable law permits. Publication and official binary distribution remain separately authorized actions. The owner approved implementation of this policy and the separate artwork copyright grant. This adoption does not authorize a commit, push, tag, release or publication of artifacts.
